messages.author: b98e21751c27e8b9
messages.subject: Re: funding for GSoC strudent to attend conference
parts:
On 12/18/2018 02:34 AM, Fisikopoulos Vissarion wrote:
> is there any GSoC funding for students of 2018 program to attend
> conferences (e.g. http://www.user2019.fr) to present their projects?

Vissarion,

Google does not provide student travel funding because GSoC is a remote
work program. This topic comes up every year at the post GSoC meeting
where the program is (among other things) discussed with Google. One
other reason that has been discussed in the past is that GSoC is also
not really 'academic', but rather a gateway or on-ramp for students to
enter the open source community.

R GSoC, not having separate funding, has not provided funding to
students to travel to conferences either.

R GSoC indirectly contributes to funding of the R Foundation, as all
non-student project stipends are sent back to the R Foundation.

I suggest that your student prominently discusses their GSoC work in
applying for other travel funding to UseR. Other former GSoC students
have had good luck with this for prior UseR!, R/Finance, StanCon, and
other conferences.

Regards,

Brian

messages.subject: Re: funding for GSoC strudent to attend conference
parts:
It is not likely a very fast possibility, but perhaps worth investigating R Consortium funding for a project
to promote / publicize R work. I've no idea what the response would be.

Mentors and alumni: It is almost certainly worth a conversation on this subject with R Consortium, since
having iron tools is no good if the users are still using flints. If you know people involved, consider asking
their opinion. Personally I wouldn't want to swamp the process with conference funding requests, but some
mechanisms for sharing knowledge is almost certainly within the mandate.

JN
